# Insert that silently skips when the idempotency key already exists

> A raw SQL insert at the start of `executePayment` that creates the `Payment` row as `PENDING` and silently does nothing if a row with the same idempotency key already exists.

_Part of [Idempotent creation of the payment row](idempotent-payment-insert.md)_

At the start of `executePayment`, inside a database transaction, the service runs a raw `INSERT INTO "Payment"`. The row gets a database-generated id (`gen_random_uuid()`), the idempotency key from the request, the amount, the user and order ids, and status `PENDING`. The statement ends with `ON CONFLICT ("idempotencyKey") DO NOTHING`. If no payment has that key yet, the row is created. If one already exists (a Kafka redelivery, a retry after a crash, or a user spamming the API), the insert quietly does nothing and raises no error. Either way, the same transaction then reads the payment back by idempotency key with `requestPayment`, so every caller ends up holding the one shared row. The status of that row decides what happens next. See [Idempotent creation of the payment row](idempotent-payment-insert.md) for the wider flow. A payment that is no longer `PENDING` or `UNKNOWN` is returned straight away. Otherwise the charge goes on. The insert relies on a unique constraint on `idempotencyKey`, which is what `ON CONFLICT` targets.

**Look at:** [`executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L53)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payment` | Row inserted with status `PENDING` and the generated id, skipped on an `idempotencyKey` conflict, then read back by idempotency key in the same transaction. |

## Also relies on

- [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md): Reads the row back through `PaymentDtoService.requestPayment` and uses the `Payment` model's `PaymentStatus` values.

## Watch out

- The insert is a raw SQL query, not a Sequelize `create`, so model defaults do not apply. The id, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are set in the SQL itself.
- `DO NOTHING` returns no error and does not say whether a row was inserted. The code always reads the row back to learn what exists.
- A duplicate message does not insert, but it gets the existing payment back. If that payment is `UNKNOWN`, it continues and re-sends to Stripe with the same key.
- Only the `idempotencyKey` conflict is ignored. A different failure, such as a bad `bisOrderId`, still raises an error.
